body.statement: Fix a stratum \(x\), a positive common kernel \(C_x\) of rank \(q=q_x\), and nonempty \(O_C(\eta_0)\). Under the rank-one row submodel, \(\operatorname{rank}(A_{P,x})=q(|V|-1)\) for \(\mu_C\)-almost every edge-row collection if and only if \(\operatorname{TreePack}_q(G)\) holds. The exceptional deficient collections are the zero set of the maximal minors of \(A_{P,x}\) in relative coordinates on \(H_C^E\). Consequently, across strata the generic global rank is \(\sum_x q_x(|V|-1)\) exactly when \(G\) packs \(q_x\) spanning trees for every \(x\).
body.justification: This theorem proves that rows genuinely attainable from a common stochastic proxy kernel realize the classical tree-packing threshold, stratum by stratum.
body.gap: The tree-packing and matroid-union certificates are classical. The new step is the nonvanishing representation theorem for constrained stochastic rows in the common-proxy image, followed by its causal rank interpretation.
body.consumer: A network designer can identify the least connectivity structure capable of attaining every contrast direction allowed by the proxies.
body.proof_tex:
Write \(k=|V|-1\) and suppress the fixed \(x\).  Every row \(c_u=C_x(u,\cdot)\) is stochastic, so the coordinate-sum functional \(\ell(t)=\sum_wt_w\) equals \(1\) on every \(c_u\).  If \(S_C=\operatorname{span}\{c_u:u\in\mathcal U\}\), then \(\dim S_C=q\), while
\[
H_C=\operatorname{aff}\{c_u\}=\{t\in S_C:\ell(t)=1\}
\]
has dimension \(q-1\).  Indeed, after fixing one row \(c_{u_0}\), the row differences span a \((q-1)\)-dimensional subspace contained in \(\ker\ell\), and \(c_{u_0}\notin\ker\ell\).

We verify that the stochastic attainability restriction does not reduce this affine dimension.  Choose \(\pi_*\in D_C(\eta_0)\), which exists by hypothesis.  All inequalities in the definition of \(D_C(\eta_0)\) are strict, so every sufficiently small \(v\) with \(\sum_uv_u=0\) has \(\pi_*+v\in D_C(\eta_0)\).  The linear map \(v\mapsto v^{\mathsf T}C_x\) maps the subspace \(\sum_uv_u=0\) onto \(H_C-H_C\), because the row differences span the latter space.  A linear surjection between finite-dimensional spaces maps a neighborhood of zero onto a neighborhood of zero: choose preimages of a basis and use the resulting linear right inverse.  Hence \(O_C(\eta_0)\) is a nonempty relatively open subset of \(H_C\), and its affine hull is \(H_C\).

Choose linear coordinates on \(S_C\) in which \(\ell\) is the first coordinate, and extend them to an invertible linear coordinate change on \(\mathbb R^d\).  Then each attainable row has coordinates
\[
t_e=(1,p_{e1},\ldots,p_{e,q-1},0,\ldots,0).
\]
All rows of \(T_{e,x}\) are copies of \(t_e\), so deleting duplicate rows does not change rank.  After the corresponding invertible column transformation, the nonzero part of \(A_{P,x}\) is
\[
\mathcal A(p)=
\bigl[B,\ \operatorname{diag}(p_{\cdot1})B,\ \ldots,
\operatorname{diag}(p_{\cdot,q-1})B\bigr],
\tag{1}
\]
where \(B\) is the reduced incidence matrix with rows \(B_e\).  The remaining \(k(d-q)\) columns are zero.

We use the elementary incidence fact that a \(k\)-row square submatrix \(B_F\) has nonzero determinant exactly when \(F\) is a spanning tree.  If \(F\) is a tree, orienting it away from the root and ordering each nonroot vertex after its parent makes \(B_F\) triangular up to row signs and permutations, with diagonal entries \(\pm1\).  If \(F\) contains a cycle, its incidence rows are dependent; if it is disconnected, the indicator of a root-free component gives a nonzero vector in the nullspace of \(B_F\).  These exhaust the non-tree cases with \(k\) edges.

Select \(qk\) edge rows in (1) and expand the corresponding determinant by its \(q\) column blocks.  Every nonzero term partitions the selected labeled edges into \(q\) sets \(F_0,\ldots,F_{q-1}\), each of size \(k\), and has coefficient
\[
\pm\prod_{j=0}^{q-1}\det(B_{F_j})
\]
times the monomial \(\prod_{j=1}^{q-1}\prod_{e\in F_j}p_{ej}\).  Distinct labeled partitions give distinct monomials: the variables in the monomial determine \(F_1,\ldots,F_{q-1}\), and the complement determines \(F_0\).  Thus cancellation between different partitions is impossible.  By the incidence fact, a nonzero determinant polynomial exists if and only if the graph contains \(q\) pairwise edge-disjoint spanning trees.

If there is no such packing, every \(qk\)-minor vanishes identically, while the proxy-rank ceiling gives rank at most \(qk\); hence the rank is always below \(qk\).  If there is a packing, its union supplies a \(qk\)-minor that is a nonzero polynomial in the relative coordinates \(p_{ej}\).  A nonzero real polynomial has a Lebesgue-null zero set.  This last fact follows by induction on the number of variables: write the polynomial as a polynomial in the last variable; outside the common zero set of its coefficient polynomials, each one-dimensional section has finitely many roots, and the induction hypothesis together with Fubini's theorem gives measure zero.  Since \(O_C(\eta_0)^E\) is relatively open in \(H_C^E\), the deficient collections are therefore the common zero set of the maximal minors and have \(\mu_C\)-measure zero.  When \(q=1\), there are no relative coordinates and (1) is \(B\); connectedness gives rank \(k\), agreeing with the zero-dimensional point-mass convention.

For finitely many covariate strata, block diagonality gives
\(\operatorname{rank}(A_P)=\sum_x\operatorname{rank}(A_{P,x})\).  Taking the finite product of the stratumwise relative measures, the intersection of the almost-sure full-rank events has probability one.  Hence the generic global rank is \(\sum_xq_x(|V|-1)\) exactly under the stated tree-packing condition in every stratum.
